19:1.sourceText: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ τὸν Ἀπολλῶ εἶναι ἐν Κορίνθῳ Παῦλον διελθόντα τὰ ἀνωτερικὰ μέρη ἐλθεῖν εἰς Ἔφεσον καὶ εὑρεῖν τινας μαθητάς,
19:1.targetText: And it came to pass, in Apollos being in Corinth, Paul having gone through the upper parts, came to Ephesus, and having found certain disciples,

groups.note: Actual ἐν with the dative article introduces the temporal articular-infinitive clause, rendered in Apollos being. Both real construction words remain together; the being infinitive retains its separate identity.
Actual ἐλθεῖν is an aorist infinitive under it came to pass, with accusative Paul as subject; English recasts that actual coming predicate as finite came.

Actual εὑρεῖν is an aorist active infinitive, while the checked TR has the aorist participle εὑρών behind having found. The actual finding head is retained without substituting the TR participial analysis.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article with Apollos has no separate English counterpart.

19:2.sourceText: εἶπέν τε πρὸς αὐτούς Εἰ Πνεῦμα Ἅγιον ἐλάβετε πιστεύσαντες; οἱ δὲ πρὸς αὐτόν Ἀλλ’ οὐδ’ εἰ Πνεῦμα Ἅγιον ἔστιν ἠκούσαμεν.
19:2.targetText: he said to them, “Having believed, did you receive the Holy Spirit?” And they said to him, “But we did not even hear whether there is any Holy Spirit”;

groups.note: Actual interrogative εἰ with the finite receiving verb forms the direct whether-or-did-you question, rendered did you receive. The first εἰ is not reassigned to the later whether clause.

unmappedSource.reason: N1904 writes the additive τε after the opening said; English starts this verse without a separate connective at that point.

unmappedTarget.reason: The checked TR additionally writes a saying verb in the reply; N1904 has the replying participants and direct speech but no second written saying predicate.
English adds this indefinite wording in the existential question; neither N1904 nor the checked TR writes an independent any word there.

19:3.sourceText: εἶπέν τε Εἰς τί οὖν ἐβαπτίσθητε; οἱ δὲ εἶπαν Εἰς τὸ Ἰωάνου βάπτισμα.
19:3.targetText: and he said to them, “Into what, then, were you immersed?” And they said, “Into John’s immersion.”

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article with John’s immersion has no separate English counterpart beside the possessive name.

unmappedTarget.reason: The checked TR has an additional προς αὐτούς addressed-recipient phrase after said; it is absent from N1904 here.

19:4.sourceText: εἶπεν δὲ Παῦλος Ἰωάνης ἐβάπτισεν βάπτισμα μετανοίας, τῷ λαῷ λέγων εἰς τὸν ἐρχόμενον μετ’ αὐτὸν ἵνα πιστεύσωσιν, τοῦτ’ ἔστιν εἰς τὸν Ἰησοῦν.
19:4.targetText: And Paul said, “John, indeed, immersed with an immersion of conversion, saying to the people that they should believe in Him who is coming after him—that is, in the Christ—Jesus”;

groups.note: Actual βάπτισμα is the accusative immersion noun in a cognate-object construction with immersed; English recasts this as with an immersion. No separate Greek with preposition is printed.
Actual μετανοίας is the genitive repentance or change-of-mind noun, rendered of conversion. Its actual μετάνοια identity is retained rather than substituting an ἐπιστροφή word.
Actual ἐρχόμενον is a present participle, rendered the relative predicate is coming. The English auxiliary belongs to this real verbal participle, not a separately printed copula.

Actual article and Jesus name form the one definite personal expression, rendered the ... Jesus with Christ explicitly explained as the additional title in the other witness. No actual Christ source identity is invented.

unmappedTarget.reason: The checked TR has an additional μέν after John; N1904 has no corresponding particle here.
The checked TR additionally titles Jesus as Christ at the end of this verse; N1904 has the article and Jesus name without a Christ-title token.

19:5.sourceText: ἀκούσαντες δὲ ἐβαπτίσθησαν εἰς τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ·
19:5.targetText: and they, having heard, were immersed into the Name of the Lord Jesus,

groups.note: The actual passive finite immersion verb is third-person plural and supplies the English subject they as well as were immersed; no independently written Greek they pronoun is asserted.

19:6.sourceText: καὶ ἐπιθέντος αὐτοῖς τοῦ Παύλου χεῖρας ἦλθε τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ Ἅγιον ἐπ’ αὐτούς, ἐλάλουν τε γλώσσαις καὶ ἐπροφήτευον.
19:6.targetText: and Paul having laid [his] hands on them, the Holy Spirit came on them, they were also speaking with tongues, and prophesying,

groups.note: Actual αὐτοῖς is the dative hand-laying recipient, rendered on them; the second on-them phrase retains its separate actual ἐπί and accusative pronoun.
Actual γλώσσαις is the dative plural tongues noun, rendered with tongues. The English with expresses that actual case construction, not an extra source preposition.
Actual ἐπροφήτευον is imperfect active indicative third-person plural; English gives prophesying in the coordinated predicate without changing the original finite analysis.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article with Paul and the repeated attributive article before Holy have no separate English counterparts.

unmappedTarget.reason: This bracketed possessive is supplied in English; the actual hands noun is anarthrous in N1904 and no independently written possessive pronoun occurs. The checked TR adds the hands article, not a personal possessive.

19:7.sourceText: ἦσαν δὲ οἱ πάντες ἄνδρες ὡσεὶ δώδεκα.
19:7.targetText: and all the men were, as it were, twelve.

19:8.sourceText: Εἰσελθὼν δὲ εἰς τὴν συναγωγὴν ἐπαρρησιάζετο ἐπὶ μῆνας τρεῖς διαλεγόμενος καὶ πείθων περὶ τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ Θεοῦ.
19:8.targetText: And having gone into the synagogue, he was speaking boldly for three months, reasoning and persuading the things concerning the Kingdom of God,

groups.note: Actual genitive article and God noun jointly supply of God; the bare English relation stays with its real nominal head.

unmappedTarget.reason: The checked TR has an additional substantivizing τὰ before concerning; N1904 has only the concerning-the-Kingdom expression at this point.

19:9.sourceText: ὡς δέ τινες ἐσκληρύνοντο καὶ ἠπείθουν κακολογοῦντες τὴν Ὁδὸν ἐνώπιον τοῦ πλήθους, ἀποστὰς ἀπ’ αὐτῶν ἀφώρισεν τοὺς μαθητάς, καθ’ ἡμέραν διαλεγόμενος ἐν τῇ σχολῇ Τυράννου.
19:9.targetText: and when certain were hardened and were disbelieving, speaking evil of The Way before the multitude, having departed from them, he separated the disciples, reasoning every day in the school of a certain Tyrannus.

groups.note: Actual ἠπείθουν is from ἀπειθέω, refusing obedience or belief, rendered were disbelieving. Its actual verb identity is retained; it is not a separately printed πιστεύω verb.
Actual κακολογοῦντες is a single evil-speaking participle, rendered speaking evil of; no independent Greek evil noun or of preposition is invented.
Actual κατά with day forms the distributive daily expression, rendered every day. Both real construction words retain one combined correspondence.
Actual Tyrannus is genitive, rendered of ... Tyrannus with the separate indefinite English addition left unpaired. The relation is not detached from its actual proper-name head.

unmappedTarget.reason: The checked TR adds an indefinite τινός with Tyrannus; N1904 has only the genitive name.

19:10.sourceText: τοῦτο δὲ ἐγένετο ἐπὶ ἔτη δύο, ὥστε πάντας τοὺς κατοικοῦντας τὴν Ἀσίαν ἀκοῦσαι τὸν λόγον τοῦ Κυρίου, Ἰουδαίους τε καὶ Ἕλληνας.
19:10.targetText: And this happened for two years so that all those dwelling in Asia heard the word of the Lord Jesus, both Jews and Greeks,

groups.note: Actual accusative article and Asia name are the inhabited-place object of dwelling; English recasts that same place as in Asia without a separately printed Greek in preposition.
Actual ἀκοῦσαι is an aorist active infinitive in the result construction; English recasts its predicate as finite heard, preserving the actual hearing head.

unmappedTarget.reason: The checked TR additionally writes Jesus after Lord; N1904 has no Jesus-name token in this verse.

19:11.sourceText: Δυνάμεις τε οὐ τὰς τυχούσας ὁ Θεὸς ἐποίει διὰ τῶν χειρῶν Παύλου,
19:11.targetText: also mighty works—not common—God was working through the hands of Paul,

groups.note: Actual article and aorist happening participle form the ordinary or commonplace expression, rendered common under not. The source τυγχάνω participle is retained, not replaced by a separately printed common adjective.
Actual ἐποίει is imperfect active indicative of ποιέω, doing or making, rendered was working. No separate ἐργάζομαι verb is printed at this occurrence.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article with God has no separate English counterpart.

19:12.sourceText: ὥστε καὶ ἐπὶ τοὺς ἀσθενοῦντας ἀποφέρεσθαι ἀπὸ τοῦ χρωτὸς αὐτοῦ σουδάρια ἢ σιμικίνθια καὶ ἀπαλλάσσεσθαι ἀπ’ αὐτῶν τὰς νόσους, τά τε πνεύματα τὰ πονηρὰ ἐκπορεύεσθαι.
19:12.targetText: so that even to the ailing were brought from his body handkerchiefs or aprons, and the diseases departed from them; the evil spirits also went forth from them.

groups.note: Actual ἀποφέρεσθαι is a present passive-function infinitive, carried away or from, with form V-PEN; checked TR uses the related ἐπιφέρεσθαι compound. English were brought retains the real carrying head while its actual infinitive and prefix remain explicit.
Actual ἀπαλλάσσεσθαι is a present passive-function infinitive, being removed, with form V-PEN; English uses finite departed. The actual passive analysis remains visible.
Actual ἐκπορεύεσθαι is a present infinitive, rendered finite went forth in the English result statement. It is not retagged as an aorist indicative.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article with his body and the repeated attributive article before evil have no separate English counterparts.

unmappedTarget.reason: The checked TR adds a second ἀπ᾽ αὐτῶν phrase with the departing spirits; N1904 has no such second phrase.

19:13.sourceText: Ἐπεχείρησαν δέ τινες καὶ τῶν περιερχομένων Ἰουδαίων ἐξορκιστῶν ὀνομάζειν ἐπὶ τοὺς ἔχοντας τὰ πνεύματα τὰ πονηρὰ τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ λέγοντες Ὁρκίζω ὑμᾶς τὸν Ἰησοῦν ὃν Παῦλος κηρύσσει.
19:13.targetText: And certain of the wandering exorcist Jews, took on [them] to name over those having the evil spirits the Name of the Lord Jesus, saying, “We adjure you by Jesus, whom Paul preaches”;

groups.note: Actual ἐπεχείρησαν is the active undertaking verb, rendered took on bracketed them as an English undertaking expression. The source is active, not an invented middle form or independently written reflexive pronoun.

Actual ὁρκίζω is present active first-person singular; the checked TR and English use a plural speaker. The actual singular verb head remains linked only to adjure, with English We separately explained.
Actual accusative article and Jesus name supply the invocation in the adjuring construction, rendered by Jesus. No independently written Greek by preposition or genitive retagging is asserted.

unmappedSource.reason: The additional Greek also particle near the opening participants has no separate English counterpart.
The repeated Greek attributive article before evil has no separate English counterpart.

unmappedTarget.reason: Actual ὁρκίζω is first-person singular, while checked TR ὁρκίζομεν is first-person plural behind English We adjure. Only the shared adjuring predicate is linked; a plural source speaker is not invented.

19:14.sourceText: ἦσαν δέ τινος Σκευᾶ Ἰουδαίου ἀρχιερέως ἑπτὰ υἱοὶ τοῦτο ποιοῦντες.
19:14.targetText: and there were certain—seven sons of Sceva, a Jew, a chief priest—who are doing this thing;

groups.note: Actual ποιοῦντες is a present active participle modifying the sons; English recasts it as the relative predicate who are doing. No independently written Greek finite copula is invented.

unmappedSource.reason: Actual τινος is genitive singular and qualifies Sceva; checked TR τινες is nominative plural and qualifies the sons behind English certain. The changed participant scope is kept as an explicit witness gap.

unmappedTarget.reason: The checked TR has nominative plural τινες for the sons; N1904 instead has genitive singular τινος with Sceva.

19:15.sourceText: ἀποκριθὲν δὲ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ πονηρὸν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Τὸν Ἰησοῦν γινώσκω καὶ τὸν Παῦλον ἐπίσταμαι· ὑμεῖς δὲ τίνες ἐστέ;
19:15.targetText: and the evil spirit, answering, said, “I know Jesus, and I am acquainted with Paul; and you—who are you?”

unmappedSource.reason: The repeated attributive article and the Greek articles with Jesus and Paul have no separate English counterparts.
N1904 additionally writes the dative reply recipient αὐτοῖς; the checked TR and this English verse omit a separate to-them expression.

19:16.sourceText: καὶ ἐφαλόμενος ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐπ’ αὐτοὺς, ἐν ᾧ ἦν τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ πονηρὸν, κατακυριεύσας ἀμφοτέρων ἴσχυσεν κατ’ αὐτῶν, ὥστε γυμνοὺς καὶ τετραυματισμένους ἐκφυγεῖν ἐκ τοῦ οἴκου ἐκείνου.
19:16.targetText: And the man, in whom was the evil spirit, leaping on them, and having overcome them, prevailed against them, so that they fled naked and wounded out of that house,

groups.note: Actual ἐκφυγεῖν is an aorist active infinitive under the result marker, rendered finite they fled; the English subject belongs to this result-clause recast, not an independently printed Greek they pronoun.

unmappedSource.reason: The repeated attributive article and the article with that house have no separate English counterparts.
Actual ἀμφοτέρων is the genitive both quantifier; checked TR instead has the personal pronoun αὐτῶν behind the second English them. The quantified and personal heads are not silently merged.

unmappedTarget.reason: The checked TR adds a connective before having overcome; N1904 juxtaposes the actual participles without that additional and.
The second English them follows the checked TR αὐτῶν; N1904 writes the different both expression ἀμφοτέρων.

19:17.sourceText: τοῦτο δὲ ἐγένετο γνωστὸν πᾶσιν Ἰουδαίοις τε καὶ Ἕλλησιν τοῖς κατοικοῦσιν τὴν Ἔφεσον, καὶ ἐπέπεσεν φόβος ἐπὶ πάντας αὐτούς, καὶ ἐμεγαλύνετο τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ·
19:17.targetText: and this became known to all, both Jews and Greeks, who are dwelling at Ephesus, and fear fell on them all, and the Name of the Lord Jesus was being magnified;

groups.note: Actual accusative article and Ephesus name are the inhabited-place object; English recasts the same place as at Ephesus, without a separately printed Greek at preposition.

19:18.sourceText: πολλοί τε τῶν πεπιστευκότων ἤρχοντο ἐξομολογούμενοι καὶ ἀναγγέλλοντες τὰς πράξεις αὐτῶν.
19:18.targetText: many also of those who believed were coming, confessing and declaring their acts,

groups.note: Actual πεπιστευκότων is a perfect active participle, rendered believed within the substantival people expression. The source perfect form is retained rather than changed to an aorist.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article with their acts has no separate English counterpart beside the possessive.

19:19.sourceText: ἱκανοὶ δὲ τῶν τὰ περίεργα πραξάντων συνενέγκαντες τὰς βίβλους κατέκαιον ἐνώπιον πάντων· καὶ συνεψήφισαν τὰς τιμὰς αὐτῶν καὶ εὗρον ἀργυρίου μυριάδας πέντε.
19:19.targetText: and many of those who had practiced the superfluous arts, having brought the scrolls together, were burning [them] before all; and they reckoned together the prices of them, and found [it] fifty thousand pieces of silver,

groups.note: Actual πραξάντων is an aorist active participle; English had practiced supplies an anterior finite-style expression without retagging the actual source participle.
Actual περίεργα is a substantival superfluous or curious adjective, rendered superfluous arts. Arts supplies English nominal support, not a separately printed Greek arts noun.
The one actual scrolls noun names the immediately brought-together and burned objects. English repeats those same objects as bracketed them; no additional source pronoun is invented.

The one actual plural prices noun supplies the values immediately reckoned together and then found as a total. English bracketed it resumes that quantified value collectively in the singular; no separately printed personal pronoun or total noun is claimed. The numeral retains its own source identity.

Actual five with the plural ten-thousand unit forms five ten-thousands, 50,000, jointly rendered fifty thousand pieces. The numerical product is kept whole rather than falsely pairing five with fifty or a ten-thousand unit with thousand alone.

19:20.sourceText: Οὕτως κατὰ κράτος τοῦ Κυρίου ὁ λόγος ηὔξανεν καὶ ἴσχυεν.
19:20.targetText: so powerfully was the word of God increasing and prevailing.

groups.note: Actual κατά with the power noun forms the adverbial according-to-power expression, rendered powerfully; both real construction words remain together.

unmappedSource.reason: N1904 and the checked printed TR have the genitive article and LORD title here, whereas this installed and pinned LSV verse says of God. No God-name source identity is invented from the unlike Lord head.

unmappedTarget.reason: The exact installed wording also appears in the pinned LSV USFM. Both N1904 and the checked printed TR instead have the Lord title; this unlike name/title expression remains unpaired without altering the Bible text.

19:21.sourceText: Ὡς δὲ ἐπληρώθη ταῦτα, ἔθετο ὁ Παῦλος ἐν τῷ πνεύματι διελθὼν τὴν Μακεδονίαν καὶ Ἀχαΐαν πορεύεσθαι εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα, εἰπὼν ὅτι Μετὰ τὸ γενέσθαι με ἐκεῖ δεῖ με καὶ Ῥώμην ἰδεῖν.
19:21.targetText: And when these things were fulfilled, Paul purposed in the Spirit, having gone through Macedonia and Achaia, to go on to Jerusalem, saying, “After my being there, it is also necessary for me to see Rome”;

groups.note: Actual ἐπληρώθη is a third-person singular passive verb with the neuter plural these things; English uses plural were fulfilled. The actual source agreement and form remain unchanged.
Actual ἔθετο is aorist middle of τίθημι, set or placed, in the in-spirit purpose expression. English purposed renders that actual setting predicate, not a separately printed intending verb.
Actual after with the accusative article introduces the articular being clause; English After my being renders its temporal construction without a separate article.
Actual με is the accusative first-person subject of the being infinitive, rendered possessive my under the English nominal being construction. It is not a source genitive pronoun.
The second actual με is the accusative subject of seeing under necessary, rendered for me. The bracket-like English for relation does not add an independent Greek preposition.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles with Paul and Macedonia have no separate English counterparts.
The Greek report particle introduces the direct words; English quotation expresses the report without a separate that.

19:22.sourceText: ἀποστείλας δὲ εἰς τὴν Μακεδονίαν δύο τῶν διακονούντων αὐτῷ, Τιμόθεον καὶ Ἔραστον, αὐτὸς ἐπέσχεν χρόνον εἰς τὴν Ἀσίαν.
19:22.targetText: and having sent to Macedonia two of those ministering to him—Timotheus and Erastus—he himself stayed a time in Asia.

groups.note: Actual αὐτός is nominative singular intensive, rendered he himself. No independent reflexive pronoun is invented.
Actual εἰς with Asia marks the place of staying here, rendered in Asia; the original preposition remains εἰς rather than being replaced by an ἐν token.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles with Macedonia and Asia have no separate English counterparts.

19:23.sourceText: Ἐγένετο δὲ κατὰ τὸν καιρὸν ἐκεῖνον τάραχος οὐκ ὀλίγος περὶ τῆς Ὁδοῦ.
19:23.targetText: And there came, at that time, not a little stir about The Way,

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article with that time has no separate English counterpart beside that.

19:24.sourceText: Δημήτριος γάρ τις ὀνόματι, ἀργυροκόπος, ποιῶν ναοὺς ἀργυροῦς Ἀρτέμιδος παρείχετο τοῖς τεχνίταις οὐκ ὀλίγην ἐργασίαν,
19:24.targetText: for a certain one, Demetrius by name, a worker in silver, making silver sanctuaries of Artemis, was bringing to the craftsmen not a little gain,

groups.note: Actual ὀνόματι is a dative name noun, rendered by name without an independently printed Greek by preposition.
Actual ἀργυροκόπος is one silversmith compound noun, rendered a worker in silver; no separate source worker and silver nouns are printed in this title.

19:25.sourceText: οὓς συναθροίσας καὶ τοὺς περὶ τὰ τοιαῦτα ἐργάτας εἶπεν Ἄνδρες, ἐπίστασθε ὅτι ἐκ ταύτης τῆς ἐργασίας ἡ εὐπορία ἡμῖν ἐστιν,
19:25.targetText: whom, having brought in a crowd together, and those who worked around such things, he said, “Men, you know that by this work we have our wealth;

targetPhrases.text: having brought in a crowd together

groups.note: Actual συναθροίσας is one gathering-together participle, rendered having brought in a crowd together. The English crowd wording belongs to this one gathering predicate, not a separately printed Greek crowd noun.
Actual ἐργάτας is the accusative plural workers noun, rendered the relative predicate who worked. Its original noun analysis remains visible; no actual working verb is substituted.

Actual wealth is to us uses the copula with the personal dative ἡμῖν; English recasts the same possession as we have our wealth. The actual copula and dative jointly express we have and the repeated same-owner our, without a separate ἔχω verb or genitive possessive token in N1904. The checked TR instead has genitive ἡμῶν in the wealth expression; the actual N1904 dative is retained.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles with this work and our wealth have no separate English counterparts beside the demonstrative and possessive.

19:26.sourceText: καὶ θεωρεῖτε καὶ ἀκούετε ὅτι οὐ μόνον Ἐφέσου ἀλλὰ σχεδὸν πάσης τῆς Ἀσίας ὁ Παῦλος οὗτος πείσας μετέστησεν ἱκανὸν ὄχλον, λέγων ὅτι οὐκ εἰσὶν θεοὶ οἱ διὰ χειρῶν γινόμενοι.
19:26.targetText: and you see and hear, that not only at Ephesus, but almost in all Asia, this Paul, having persuaded, turned away a great multitude, saying that they who are made by hands are not gods;

groups.note: Actual Ephesus is a genitive place expression, rendered at Ephesus; no separately printed Greek at preposition is claimed.
Actual genitive article and Asia name supply the same territorial scope, rendered in ... Asia with all separately anchored. The English in is not treated as a standalone article lemma.
Actual γινόμενοι is a present participle of γίνομαι, coming into being, rendered are made. Its actual V-PNP-NPM analysis is retained, not replaced by a passive ποιέω form.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article with this Paul has no separate English counterpart beside this.

19:27.sourceText: οὐ μόνον δὲ τοῦτο κινδυνεύει ἡμῖν τὸ μέρος εἰς ἀπελεγμὸν ἐλθεῖν, ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸ τῆς μεγάλης θεᾶς Ἀρτέμιδος ἱερὸν εἰς οὐθὲν λογισθῆναι, μέλλειν τε καὶ καθαιρεῖσθαι τῆς μεγαλειότητος αὐτῆς, ἣν ὅλη ἡ Ἀσία καὶ ἡ οἰκουμένη σέβεται.
19:27.targetText: and not only is this department in danger for us of coming into disregard, but also, that of the great goddess Artemis, the temple is to be reckoned for nothing, and also her greatness is about to be brought down, whom all Asia and the world worships.”

groups.note: The one actual article introduces the same temple phrase. English preposes that of the goddess and resumes the named temple with the; these are two English determiner pieces for the one original nominal construction, not two written Greek articles.

Actual λογισθῆναι is an aorist passive infinitive, rendered the finite-style temple predicate is to be reckoned. The real infinitive supplies the English verbal auxiliaries without an independently printed source copula.

Actual μεγαλειότητος is genitive in both pinned analyses, while the checked TR has accusative μεγαλειότητα. English recasts greatness as the explicit subject of being brought down; its actual genitive source form is retained without assigning it an accusative tag.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles with this department, her greatness, and all Asia have no separate English counterparts beside those English modifiers.

19:28.sourceText: Ἀκούσαντες δὲ καὶ γενόμενοι πλήρεις θυμοῦ ἔκραζον λέγοντες Μεγάλη ἡ Ἄρτεμις Ἐφεσίων.
19:28.targetText: And having heard, and having become full of wrath, they were crying out, saying, “Great [is] the Artemis of the Ephesians!”

unmappedTarget.reason: The bracketed copula in the quoted great-Artemis acclamation is supplied in English; neither N1904 nor the checked TR writes a being word there.

19:29.sourceText: καὶ ἐπλήσθη ἡ πόλις τῆς συγχύσεως, ὥρμησάν τε ὁμοθυμαδὸν εἰς τὸ θέατρον, συναρπάσαντες Γάϊον καὶ Ἀρίσταρχον Μακεδόνας, συνεκδήμους Παύλου.
19:29.targetText: And the whole city was filled with confusion; they rushed also with one accord into the theater, having caught Gaius and Aristarchus, Macedonians, Paul’s fellow-travelers.

groups.note: Actual genitive article and confusion noun supply the filling content, rendered with confusion. The English with is retained with the real case-bearing nominal head, not an invented Greek preposition.
Actual Μακεδόνας is an ethnic noun, recorded N-APM, rendered Macedonians. The original noun tag is not replaced by an adjective analysis.

unmappedTarget.reason: The checked TR additionally writes ὅλη with city; N1904 has no whole quantifier at this point.

19:30.sourceText: Παύλου δὲ βουλομένου εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὸν δῆμον οὐκ εἴων αὐτὸν οἱ μαθηταί·
19:30.targetText: And on Paul’s resolving to enter in to the populace, the disciples were not permitting him,

groups.note: The actual genitive resolving participle with genitive Paul forms the circumstance clause; English on expresses its temporal relation without a separately printed Greek on preposition.

19:31.sourceText: τινὲς δὲ καὶ τῶν Ἀσιαρχῶν, ὄντες αὐτῷ φίλοι, πέμψαντες πρὸς αὐτὸν παρεκάλουν μὴ δοῦναι ἑαυτὸν εἰς τὸ θέατρον.
19:31.targetText: and also some of the chief men of Asia, being his friends, having sent to him, were pleading [with] him not to venture into the theater himself.

groups.note: Actual Ἀσιαρχῶν is the one Asiarch title noun, rendered chief men of Asia; the English chief, men, and Asia words are components of that title rendering, not separately printed source words.
Actual αὐτῷ is the dative friendship participant, rendered possessive his under friends. It is not an independently printed genitive possessive pronoun.
Actual φίλοι is a substantival friend adjective, recorded A-NPM, rendered friends. The original adjective analysis is retained.

The one actual accusative αὐτόν is the person addressed by the sent message and the immediate plea not to enter. English repeats him across sent to him and pleading with him; no second source personal pronoun is invented.
Actual παρακαλέω is the pleading or urging predicate; English with is verbal-complement support under pleading with the same person, not a separately printed Greek with preposition.

Actual δοῦναι with the written reflexive and into-the-theater expression is the giving-oneself-into construction, rendered to venture ... himself. The actual source is an aorist infinitive of δίδωμι, not a separately printed venturing verb.

19:32.sourceText: ἄλλοι μὲν οὖν ἄλλο τι ἔκραζον· ἦν γὰρ ἡ ἐκκλησία συγκεχυμένη, καὶ οἱ πλείους οὐκ ᾔδεισαν τίνος ἕνεκα συνεληλύθεισαν.
19:32.targetText: Some indeed, therefore, were calling out one thing, and some another, for the assembly was confused, and the greater part did not know for what they had come together;

groups.note: Actual ἄλλοι ... ἄλλο τι is the correlated other-people/other-thing distributive construction. English expands the one printed pattern as Some ... one thing, and some another; no second Greek participant, object, or conjunction is manufactured.
Actual article and comparative plural greater adjective form the majority expression, rendered the greater part. Part is English nominal support rather than a separately written Greek part noun.
Actual ᾔδεισαν is pluperfect active third-person plural, rendered did know under not. The actual source form remains pluperfect rather than an invented aorist.

19:33.sourceText: ἐκ δὲ τοῦ ὄχλου συνεβίβασαν Ἀλέξανδρον, προβαλόντων αὐτὸν τῶν Ἰουδαίων· ὁ δὲ Ἀλέξανδρος κατασείσας τὴν χεῖρα ἤθελεν ἀπολογεῖσθαι τῷ δήμῳ.
19:33.targetText: and out of the multitude they put forward Alexander—the Jews thrusting him forward—and Alexander having beckoned with the hand, wished to make defense to the populace,

groups.note: Actual accusative definite hand expression is the gesture instrument under beckoned, rendered with the hand. The real nominal head remains with this English instrumental recast; no independent with preposition is printed.

unmappedSource.reason: Actual συνεβίβασαν is from συμβιβάζω, bringing together, prompting, or instructing; the checked TR instead has προεβίβασαν, putting forward. The different predicate heads are not forced into one exact lexical link. Primary dictionary: https://www.billmounce.com/greek-dictionary/symbibazo .
The Greek article with the second Alexander name has no separate English counterpart.

unmappedTarget.reason: This follows the checked TR προεβίβασαν; N1904 instead writes the different συνεβίβασαν predicate.

19:34.sourceText: ἐπιγνόντες δὲ ὅτι Ἰουδαῖός ἐστιν, φωνὴ ἐγένετο μία ἐκ πάντων, ὡς ἐπὶ ὥρας δύο κράζοντες Μεγάλη ἡ Ἄρτεμις Ἐφεσίων.
19:34.targetText: and having known that he is a Jew, one voice came out of all, for about two hours, crying, “Great [is] the Artemis of the Ephesians!”

groups.note: Actual ἐπιγνόντες is a nominative plural aorist participle; the checked TR has genitive ἐπιγνόντων. The English knowing predicate keeps its actual nominative analysis.

unmappedTarget.reason: The bracketed copula in the repeated great-Artemis acclamation is supplied in English; no Greek being word is written in that nominal acclamation.

19:35.sourceText: καταστείλας δὲ ὁ γραμματεὺς τὸν ὄχλον φησίν Ἄνδρες Ἐφέσιοι, τίς γάρ ἐστιν ἀνθρώπων ὃς οὐ γινώσκει τὴν Ἐφεσίων πόλιν νεωκόρον οὖσαν τῆς μεγάλης Ἀρτέμιδος καὶ τοῦ διοπετοῦς;
19:35.targetText: And the public clerk having quieted the multitude, says, “Men, Ephesians, why, who is the man that does not know that the city of the Ephesians is temple-keeper of the great goddess Artemis, and of that which fell down from Zeus?

groups.note: Actual γάρ is the explanatory discourse particle, rendered the English introductory why. This is not an independently printed Greek why-question word.

Actual ἀνθρώπων is genitive plural, of people, while checked TR has singular nominative ἄνθρωπος. English the man recasts the personal-class expression in the who-is question; the source retains its actual genitive plural noun analysis.

Actual οὖσαν is the accusative being participle with the known city; English recasts that content as a finite that ... is clause. No independent Greek that conjunction or finite being word is invented at this location.
Actual νεωκόρον is the one temple-keeper title noun, recorded N-ASM, rendered temple-keeper. Primary dictionary: https://www.billmounce.com/greek-dictionary/neokoros .

targetPhrases.text: of that which fell down from Zeus

groups.note: Actual genitive article and substantival Zeus-fallen adjective jointly supply of that which fell down from Zeus. The relative-clause English expands one original adjective; there are no separate printed source falling verb or Zeus-name tokens here. Primary dictionary: https://www.billmounce.com/greek-dictionary/diopetes .

unmappedTarget.reason: The checked TR explicitly writes a goddess noun with Artemis here; N1904 has only the great-Artemis expression without that noun.

19:36.sourceText: ἀναντιρρήτων οὖν ὄντων τούτων δέον ἐστὶν ὑμᾶς κατεσταλμένους ὑπάρχειν καὶ μηδὲν προπετὲς πράσσειν.
19:36.targetText: These things, then, being undeniable, it is necessary for you to be quiet, and to do nothing rashly.

groups.note: Actual necessary participle δέον with the written copula ἐστιν forms it is necessary. Both real source words remain together; no nominal adjective is assigned an unwritten copula.
Actual ὑμᾶς is the accusative subject of the following being and doing infinitives, rendered for you; no independent for preposition is printed.
Actual κατεσταλμένους is a perfect passive quieted participle, rendered quiet. Its actual verbal participle analysis is retained rather than replaced by an adjective tag.
Actual προπετές is a neuter accusative rash adjective under nothing, rendered adverbially as rashly. Its recorded A-ASN analysis is retained, not replaced by a source ADV tag.

19:37.sourceText: ἠγάγετε γὰρ τοὺς ἄνδρας τούτους οὔτε ἱεροσύλους οὔτε βλασφημοῦντας τὴν θεὸν ἡμῶν.
19:37.targetText: For you brought these men, who are neither temple-robbers nor slandering of your goddess;

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles with these men and the possessed goddess expression have no separate English counterparts.
Actual ἡμῶν is first-person plural our; the checked TR instead has second-person plural ὑμῶν behind English your. The differing possessive persons remain explicit gaps.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the relative/copular frame before the nominal temple-robber predicate; neither N1904 nor the checked TR writes an independent relative or being word there.
This follows the checked TR second-person possessive ὑμῶν; N1904 writes first-person ἡμῶν, our.

19:38.sourceText: εἰ μὲν οὖν Δημήτριος καὶ οἱ σὺν αὐτῷ τεχνῖται ἔχουσι πρός τινα λόγον, ἀγοραῖοι ἄγονται καὶ ἀνθύπατοί εἰσιν, ἐγκαλείτωσαν ἀλλήλοις.
19:38.targetText: if indeed, therefore, Demetrius and the craftsmen with him have a matter with anyone, court [days] are held, and there are proconsuls; let them accuse one another.

groups.note: Actual ἀγοραῖοι is a feminine plural court adjective, used with an understood day or session noun; English court bracketed days supplies that nominal support without inventing a written Greek days noun. Primary dictionary: https://www.billmounce.com/greek-dictionary/agoraios .
Actual ἐγκαλείτωσαν is a third-person plural imperative, rendered let them accuse. Let and them express that actual imperative construction, not separately printed Greek permission or person words.

19:39.sourceText: εἰ δέ τι περαιτέρω ἐπιζητεῖτε, ἐν τῇ ἐννόμῳ ἐκκλησίᾳ ἐπιλυθήσεται.
19:39.targetText: And if you seek after anything concerning other matters, it will be determined in the legal assembly;

unmappedSource.reason: Actual περαιτέρω is the comparative further adverb, whereas the checked TR writes the distinct περί ἑτέρων, concerning other matters, expression. The unlike printed heads are kept explicitly unpaired.

unmappedTarget.reason: This follows the checked TR περί ἑτέρων; N1904 instead has the further adverb περαιτέρω.

19:40.sourceText: καὶ γὰρ κινδυνεύομεν ἐγκαλεῖσθαι στάσεως περὶ τῆς σήμερον, μηδενὸς αἰτίου ὑπάρχοντος, περὶ οὗ οὐ δυνησόμεθα ἀποδοῦναι λόγον περὶ τῆς συστροφῆς ταύτης. καὶ ταῦτα εἰπὼν ἀπέλυσεν τὴν ἐκκλησίαν.
19:40.targetText: for we are also in peril of being accused of insurrection in regard to this day, there being no occasion by which we will be able to give an account of this concourse”;

groups.note: Actual ἐγκαλεῖσθαι is a present passive-function infinitive with form V-PEN, rendered of being accused. The English of belongs to the peril-complement construction, not an independent Greek of preposition.
Actual genitive article with the today adverb forms the this-day temporal expression. No independently printed Greek this demonstrative or day noun is invented.
Actual αἰτίου is a substantival cause adjective, recorded A-GSN, rendered occasion. The original adjective analysis is retained.
Actual περί with the genitive relative forms the concerning-which relation, rendered by which. This records the named English relational recast without inventing a Greek by preposition.

unmappedSource.reason: N1904 writes a negative οὐ before the future ability verb; the checked TR and this English clause omit that negative. The actual negative is not reassigned to another clause or silently turned positive.
The Greek article with this concourse has no separate English counterpart beside this.

sourceMoved.reason: The six actual N1904 words concluding raw19:40 are rendered at LSV19:41. They retain raw19:40 source identities rather than an invented Greek19:41.

19:41.targetText: and having said these things, he dismissed the assembly.

groups.note: This complete closing clause belongs to raw N1904 19:40 and is rendered at LSV19:41. Every group keeps its true 19:40 reference; no Greek19:41 is fabricated.
